messages:
maria: Running @redwood/inference-js in an Expo managed app (prebuild + EAS). Metro fails: "Unable to resolve "crypto"" and TS yells about ReadableStream. Anyone hit this?
kevin: Is this Expo Go or a built app via EAS?
maria: EAS prebuild -> iOS simulator. Bundler fails when app does `import {createClient} from '@redwood/inference-js'` because our node entry imports `crypto`.
jasmin: Node core modules in RN are the usual trouble. We need a react-native entry that uses expo-random or react-native-get-random-values. Also RN doesn't provide ReadableStream types.
kevin: Options: (1) conditional exports + `react-native` field in package.json pointing to a tiny RN shim, (2) avoid exposing ReadableStream in public TS types (use AsyncIterable), (3) example Expo app in `examples/` to CI-validate packaging.
maria: I tried adding `react-native` in package.json but Metro still resolved our CJS main. Any tips on exports map that Metro respects?
jasmin: Metro doesn't honor exports conditions the same way Node does. Two pragmatic approaches: add a top-level `react-native` field in package.json (point to dist/rn/index.js) AND publish a `@redwood/inference-js/react-native` subpath so apps can explicitly import the RN build.
kevin: For runtime randomness, prefer expo-random in docs. Runtime fix for some folks is `import 'react-native-get-random-values'` at app entry so `global.crypto.getRandomValues` exists. But we shouldn't force that on users if we can shim in our RN build.
maria: TypeScript: many RN projects exclude dom libs, so exporting ReadableStream in types breaks them. Switching streaming signatures to `AsyncIterable<Uint8Array | string>` sounds safer. We can provide a helper `toReadableStream()` for environments that have it.
jasmin: Agreed. Also add a small `types/rn.d.ts` to avoid requiring `dom` lib. Keep public typings RN-friendly.
kevin: For edge/Cloudflare workers, ensure the ESM edge build is free of node-only imports. Add an `exports` condition for `worker` or `edge` that points at dist/edge/index.mjs.
maria: I pushed a tiny PR: RN shim + type changes + docs. CI integration failing on the Expo example due to unresolved `crypto` in metro. bot-ci posted the logs.
bot-ci: PR #412 integration failed: metro bundling unresolved `crypto`. See logs: https://ci.internal/412/metro.log
anny: I hit runtime error on Android: `global.crypto.getRandomValues` is undefined — fixed by top-level import of `react-native-get-random-values`. Document that as a stopgap.
maria: Will update README with steps: `expo install expo-random` or `yarn add react-native-get-random-values` + import at app root. Also add CI job that runs `expo prebuild` + metro bundler for examples.
kevin: Small packaging nits: add `optionalDependencies` for `expo-random` to hint users, and ensure RN build target is es2019. Also remove direct `crypto` imports from files that may be bundled into RN entry.
jasmin: When publishing, mark the RN entry as tiny and avoid including `crypto-browserify`. Folks on low bandwidth RN apps will thank us.
maria: Thanks — I'll iterate on the PR. If you see the CI log or hit other errors (stack traces, emulator/os), drop them here.
